description: The image displays four pie charts comparing the distribution of error types across four different language models — GPT-4-0, Gemini 1.5, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct — as evaluated in the FactBench benchmark for factuality. Each chart breaks down errors into categories such as “Lack of Knowledge,” “Misinformation,” “Safety,” “Ethical Advice,” and “Clarification,” with percentages and absolute counts shown for each segment. In GPT-4-0, “Lack of Knowledge” dominates at 83.3% (5 instances), with “Safety” at 16.7% (1 instance). Gemini 1.5 shows a more diverse error profile: “Misinformation” is largest at 38.4% (33 instances), followed by “Lack of Knowledge” at 22.1% (19), “Ethical Advice” at 16.3% (14), “Clarification” at 14.0% (12), and “Safety” at 9.3% (8). Llama3.1-70B-Instruct is primarily affected by “Lack of Knowledge” at 75.0% (3 instances), with “Clarification” at 25.0% (1 instance). Llama3.1-405B-Instruct splits evenly between “Lack of Knowledge” and “Misinformation,” each at 50.0% (2 instances each). The charts use distinct colors for each category and label slices with both percentage and count, allowing for direct comparison of error composition across models.
